m1.quote: Genuinely good practices are listed (bcrypt for machine secrets, SHA-256 token digests, AES-GCM for refresh tokens, rate limiting before bcrypt cost, fail-closed persona defaults), but none of this has been externally attested (no third-party pentest or audit is mentioned, only OpenSSF Scorecard/CodeQL/Semgrep, which are automated static tools, not human security review).
m1.note: Asserts the security-critical code has had no human review or audit and ties concentrated risk to a small team, beyond a generic bus-factor concern.

m2.quote: **Running your own OAuth 2.1 authorization server** is inherently a bigger attack surface and operational responsibility than delegating fully to an existing IdP's client registration flow, even if justified by MCP spec requirements.
m2.note: Frames the built-in authorization server as home-grown auth that should have been delegated to an IdP, calling it a 'reimplement[ed] pass-through'.

m3.note: Engages directly with the Zenodo/DOI benchmark and critiques it as self-authored and single-model rather than claiming evidence is absent.

m4.note: Correctly notes DataHub is optional and only the headline enrichment benchmark depends on it; the lock-in bullet is about platform-written metadata, not DataHub as a hard requirement.
